title: 2D Offset: the planner cuts into the part wall - it does not keep the tool offset from the edge boundary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-22, in his own words:

> bug; operation is cutting into part when its planning its movements; its not a user setting but the planner not respecting the edge boundary and offsetting the tool correctly

He sent a screenshot of the Simulate view. It is not attached here.

## What happens

The generated toolpath cuts into the part. The planner does not keep the tool at its offset from the edge boundary. This is not a setting that the user chose. It is the planner.

## What the screenshot shows

- A close view of the viewport in Simulate. The part is a raised island with a figure-8 outline. The tool stands next to the island.
- A broad orange band runs along the wall of the part, at the top edge, around the curved outline. The maintainer reads this band as the cut into the part. The worker confirms what the orange marks in this build.
- The build is v0.25.0 (commit 7e2a8119). The operation is the same `2D Offset1` as in #3316 and #3319: model `fig8`, tool `EM-0800-4FL` (Ø8), Outside containment, Clearance Z32, Top Z22, Bottom Z1.5, Stepdown 10.

## Link to the other defects of this operation

The operation page shows the warning `move 522 cuts past the finish surface - repeated on 62 more moves (to 1710)`. That warning is the same defect: the moves 522 to 1710 go past the finish surface. It is a separate defect from the slotting of #3316 (the ring order) and from the three rapids of #3319. The ring order may put the tool near the wall, but the offset of the tool from the boundary is wrong whatever the order.

## Expected

For an "Outside" containment, the tool centre stays one tool radius (4.000 mm for the Ø8 tool) plus the boundary offset away from the part edge. The tool never goes past the finish surface. The generator never makes a path that its own verify check refuses.

## Priority and safety

The verify check flags the moves and the post is blocked. So no cut into the part posts today. The planner still makes a path that cuts into the part. The maintainer did not name a priority. The issue is P2 because the post is blocked. The maintainer can raise it to P1.

If the fix changes the offset geometry or the ring order, it is under the safety floor: the pin goes red first, and the review is an independent Opus read with a hand trace of one move.

## Where to look

- The offset of the boundary by the tool radius for the Outside band, and the corner handling of the figure-8 outline (two concave arcs).
- The code of `crates/motion/src/machining2d/` for the 2D Offset kind.
- The test `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (the known-fail pin of #2849) uses the same model and tool. Its body says the last feed ends 31.406 mm from the outline where 4 mm is expected. The worker checks if it is the same defect.

Done means: a pin test on `fig8.step` with `EM-0800-4FL` (Outside, the heights above) shows no move closer to the part than the tool radius, and the verify check gives no `cuts past the finish surface` warning; every shipped golden is byte-identical; an independent Opus read and a hand trace of one move near a concave arc.
